Label: Guarded Political Distrust
Description: This segment tends toward moderate trust (rating of 4) in most national institutions, including the justice system, auditor, and supreme court. However, they express notably lower trust in political parties and the police, with higher probabilities of selecting 'not at all' or low ratings (1-3) for these institutions.

Label: Moderate, Reserved Trust
Description: This segment generally expresses moderate trust in most national institutions, with response probabilities peaking around 5 or 6 on the seven-point scale. While outright distrust (ratings of 1 or 2) is rare across institutions, strong trust (ratings of 7) is also uncommon, suggesting a cautious or reserved level of confidence.

Label: Widespread Institutional Distrust
Description: This segment is characterized by low trust across nearly all national institutions, with probabilities exceeding 0.60 for 'not at all' (Nada) for most. Political parties stand out as particularly distrusted, with an 86% probability of a 'not at all' response.

Label: Cautious, Moderate Trust
Description: This segment generally expresses moderate levels of trust in most national institutions, frequently selecting '3' as their response. However, they exhibit notably lower trust in the police and political parties, with a high probability of responding 'Nada' (not at all) for these institutions.

Label: High Presidential Trust
Description: This segment expresses strong trust in the president (82% give a 'lot' of trust) and generally high trust in the justice system, electoral tribunal, armed forces, public ministry, and supreme court (all above 70% 'a lot'). While trust is lower in other institutions, this segment avoids expressing 'not at all' distrust across most items.
